chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: The soundie 'Hot in the Groove'
summary: He barely remembers the 1942 film and thinks it reused earlier footage.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: There was a 1942 movie, a 3 minute movie, an actual soundie called Hot In The Groove. A 3 minute movie. Do you remember that one?
No. I can't place that right now.
Because that was one that you....
in that? Hot In The Groove? Hot In The Groove. Right. It's a 3 minute film, an actual sound. It was 1942, and there's a question mark over '42. I was wondering if you had any memories of that one.
Let's see. It's a, right. It's a soundie featuring Erskine Hawkins and his orchestra. You see "Hot Nocturne" and also "Blues In The Night".
Okay. [INTERRUPTION] We were talking about that soundie, Hot In The Groove, from 1942, which had "Hot Nocturne" and "Blues In The Night".

In the, here it says that, 'The soundie was a short film produced, and was spooled together and projected one at a time by way of a complicated series of reflectors onto the rear of a glass screen.' What was that like?

I can remember about that was part of it was taken from the short that I made, you know, and put together in there because I don't remember making something special for that. The next thing I saw seemed like one of the scenes from the show that I did on that soundie.
